# Documentation standard

numb-form documents itself the way OpenBSD and FreeBSD do.
The manual is part of the program: a change is not finished until the
manual describes it.

Sources: OpenBSD [mdoc(7)](https://man.openbsd.org/mdoc.7) and its
[problem report](https://www.openbsd.org/report.html) page, FreeBSD
[style.mdoc(5)](https://man.freebsd.org/style.mdoc), the
[FreeBSD Documentation Project Primer](https://docs.freebsd.org/en/books/fdp-primer/)
and the
[FreeBSD Committer's Guide](https://docs.freebsd.org/en/articles/committers-guide/)
(`Relnotes:`, `RELNOTES`, `UPDATING`).

## Rules

1. **The manual changes with the code.**
   A pull request that changes what a person sees or does changes the
   manual page that describes it, in the same pull request.
   This covers programs, subcommands, flags, prompts, messages, defaults,
   configuration keys, files read or written, exit statuses and release
   files.
2. **A documentation error is a bug.**
   Wrong, missing or unclear documentation is reported and fixed like a
   bug in the code.
3. **Every release says what changed.**
   A pull request that changes the programs adds its lines to
   [CHANGES.md](../CHANGES.md), under the version it will be released
   as.
   What users must do after updating goes under **Action needed**.
4. **English is the source.**
   `docs/es` and `docs/de` are generated by the translate workflow and
   never edited by hand.
5. **No real customer data.**
   Examples use made-up names: `Foo GmbH`, `Bar S.A.`, `D10629 Foo S.A.`.

CI enforces what a program can check:

| Check | Where |
| --- | --- |
| every flag of every program appears as `` `-flag` `` in the English documentation | `TestFlagsDocumented` in `docs_test.go` |
| every configuration key has an entry `` `key = ...` `` in `docs/configuration.md` | `TestKeysDocumented` |
| every relative link in the English documentation resolves | `TestLinksResolve` |
| a pull request that changes the programs changes `CHANGES.md` | `scripts/check-changes.sh`, ci job *changes listed* |
| the install commands match `scripts/install` (templates and the pinned release) | `TestInstallCommandsPinned` |
| the documented Linux commands work on every listed distribution (minor releases) | `.github/workflows/linux.yml` |

Install commands between `<!-- install:NAME -->` markers are generated.
Edit `scripts/install/templates/NAME.*` and run
`go run ./scripts/install render`, never the documents.

## Manual pages

Each program has one manual page in `docs/`, named after the program
(`usage.md` is numb-form's), and the configuration file has its own
(`configuration.md`, NUMB-FORM.CONF(5)).
`numb-form man` shows them; add new pages to `internal/manual` and to
the `SOURCES` of `.github/translate/translate.py`.

The title is the program in capitals with its section:
`# NUMB-FORM(1)`.
The sections follow the order of mdoc(7); leave out those that do not
apply:

| Section | Contents |
| --- | --- |
| NAME | the program and a one-line description |
| SYNOPSIS | every form of the command line |
| DESCRIPTION | what the program does, step by step |
| COMMANDS | subcommands |
| OPTIONS | every flag, alphabetically |
| ENVIRONMENT | environment variables it reads |
| FILES | every file it reads or writes, with its path |
| EXIT STATUS | every exit code and its meaning |
| EXAMPLES | complete, labelled commands |
| DIAGNOSTICS | messages, exactly as printed, and what to do |
| SEE ALSO | related pages |
| HISTORY | the version that introduced the program or a major change |
| CAVEATS | surprising behaviour that is not a bug |
| BUGS | known bugs |
| SECURITY CONSIDERATIONS | what the program protects and what it trusts |

## Two kinds of reader

**People who are not technical** read [the guide](../docs/guide.md).
It assumes Windows, numbers every step, shows every question and what
to answer, explains every word it uses and says what to do when
something goes wrong.
Anything a person must do to use the programs is in the guide.

**Everyone else** reads the manual pages, which are complete and terse.
The guide links to them for details; it never contradicts them.

## Style

* Write short declarative sentences in the present tense.
  Give instructions in the imperative: "Type `numb-form`", not "You
  should type".
* Start each sentence on a new line in the Markdown source (mdoc(7)).
  Diffs then show which sentence changed.
* Do not use contractions.
  Use the serial comma: "the name, the address, and the date"
  (FreeBSD Primer).
* Do not use em dashes, en dashes or semicolons in new text.
  Use a period or a comma.
* No marketing, no "simply", "just", "easy" or "powerful".
* Quote messages exactly as the program prints them, in backticks.
* Write every procedure as a single command, labelled **Unix-like**
  (macOS, Linux, BSD; joined with `&&`) or **Windows** (10, 11;
  PowerShell 5.1, joined with `;` and `if ($?) { }`, or one `& { ... }`
  block), or say that it is the same on all systems.
* Name keys as people see them: **Enter**, **Ctrl+C**.

## Checklist for a pull request

* [ ] The manual page of every changed behaviour is updated.
* [ ] New messages appear under DIAGNOSTICS or in the guide's *When
      something goes wrong*.
* [ ] `CHANGES.md` has the change, and **Action needed** if users must
      act.
* [ ] The guide still matches what a person sees.
* [ ] Examples use made-up names only.
